post.0:
I finished third with 47; Ben ran away with 93 and Cal took second with 69. The game turned in round II when Cal ran Demote then Promote on my members: he took Line Cutters, handed me back cheaper bodies, and Recruiter paid him +2 red on each swap, flipping a red contest I led 8-4 into his 14-8 and stealing the first seat I had just drawn off Walk-In. Meanwhile Ben's white engine (Money Changers refunding every buy, Allowance into Dyer and Heiresses, then Farewell and Estate Sale casting out spent members for their full cost) compounded every round and nobody had a lever on white. My patient engine plan never got going: the cheap members that pay every round never showed for me, and I misread Guest Book, since holding Dabblers (wild) meant Mentor and Go-Between never counted as new colors, so I lost the +4 yellow I paid for. I salvaged the round III yellow +10 by sweeping all five yellow spaces I could reach, but I also misclicked a Dilute and gave Cal yellow instead of red.
FEEL: Allowance | 3 | 3 | yes | solid white gain with a member bonus; Ben used it well, I never got there first.
FEEL: Splurge | 2 | 2 | yes | rarely beat Exchange or a straight buy for me; only good when you're already buying a pricey member.
FEEL: Exchange | 4 | 4 | yes | the best follower rate on the wheel, 2 for 1, and I took it every round I could.
FEEL: Farewell | 4 | 3 | yes | casting a spent once-per-game member for its full cost in followers is too generous; Dyer paid Ben 7.
FEEL: Estate Sale | 4 | 2 | yes | Heiresses paying 7 white on use and then 9 white again on cast-out felt like a loophole from across the table.
FEEL: Cash In | 3 | 3 | yes | a clean finisher for whoever holds white; no dilemma, just Ben's payday.
FEEL: Tryout | 3 | 3 | yes | flexible; using Cashier's On Recruit for a free follower was a nice small play.
FEEL: Gather | 3 | 3 | yes | honest red plus a member kicker; I took it mostly to keep red, which then didn't matter.
FEEL: Walk-In | 4 | 5 | yes | flipping Line Cutters for free was my highlight; seeing Old Maid on top later made it a trap, which is fun table texture.
FEEL: Promote | 5 | 1 | yes | with Recruiter and Deprogrammers it's the strongest space on the board; being the target felt awful and I had no counter.
FEEL: Demote | 5 | 1 | yes | same as Promote; the pair in one round swung +10 red to Cal and took my first seat.
FEEL: Recruit a Member | 3 | 3 | yes | a free member up to 8 is good; Cal used it for Patriarch, which then paid 8.
FEEL: Harvest | 4 | 4 | yes | biggest raw gain each round and the space I fought hardest for; any-color makes it a contest lever.
FEEL: Trade Seeds | 3 | 3 | yes | I took it in round III mostly to deny Ben a yellow climb; fine, not exciting.
FEEL: Dilute | 4 | 3 | yes | Ben's round I Dilute turned my yellow into red and handed me the red lead, so it cuts both ways, which I liked.
FEEL: Big Dilute | 4 | 4 | yes | six changes can swing two contests at once; it knocked Cal off red briefly and made yellow mine.
FEEL: Melting Pot | 3 | 3 | yes | decent resource haul; I took it to close off Cal's route to yellow.
FEEL: Makeover | 4 | 3 | yes | huge for whoever has a big pile; Ben's pivot into Heiresses showed it.
FEEL: Guest Book | 2 | 2 | yes | +2 yellow per new color sounded like my plan, but wild Dabblers silently ate the trigger; only fired once all game.
FEEL: Recruiter | 5 | 2 | unsure | the artifact I'd least want to face: it pays the swapper on their own Promote/Demote, so it's a red engine aimed at your neighbors.
FEEL: Money Changers | 5 | 3 | yes | Ben's whole engine; every buy anyone makes feeds white, so the white contest is decided at the draft.
FEEL: Drifters | 3 | 4 | yes | 3 for 2 bodies and a color choice; a good round I buy.
FEEL: Line Cutters | 3 | 4 | unsure | free off Walk-In and great, until Cal swapped it away the same round.
FEEL: Mentor & Protégés | 4 | 3 | yes | 9 for 3 bodies plus a free cheapest member is fair; I bought it for Guest Book, which didn't fire.
FEEL: Go-Between | 2 | 2 | yes | arrived free; the one-color tweak almost never mattered.
FEEL: Dabblers | 2 | 1 | unsure | arrived via Cal's swap and quietly killed my Guest Book triggers; wild members need a reminder text against new-color effects.
FEEL: Scouts | 1 | 1 | unsure | came to me by swap in round III; never used.
FEEL: Mob | 3 | 2 | yes | 12 cost for 5 bodies and about 6 followers, worse than buying 10 straight; I weighed it and passed.
FEEL: HR | 2 | 2 | unsure | 10 for 4 bodies, only good with three of a color, which nobody had.
FEEL: Extra Hand | 3 | 2 | unsure | at 9 on the last turn, an extra placement plus a recruit still lost to buying 10 followers.
FEEL: Ringleader | 3 | 3 | yes | I weighed it to tie Cal's red; it would have stranded 7 resources.
FEEL: Cashier | 2 | 3 | yes | only touched it through Tryout for a free follower; fine.
META: Contests and the follower buy are the whole game; most members cost more than their followers plus ability, so by round III everyone is just buying 10 for 10, and the patient engine plan has no cheap engines to run. The Red swap spaces with Recruiter and Deprogrammers are the most punishing thing on the table, and the White cast-out spaces paying full cost for spent once-per-game members are the biggest loophole. First change: Farewell and Estate Sale should pay half the cost (or nothing for a member whose once-per-game is spent), and Recruiter should not pay on the owner's own swaps.
post.1:
I won 93 to 69 to 47, and I think it came down to two things: blocking both yellow swap spaces in rounds I and II, and owning white every round with Money Changers. Dilute followed by Trade Seeds on my double turn took Ava's yellow and then Cal's yellow away, and left nobody a space to swap back, which gave me four of the six contests in the first two rounds. After that Money Changers turned every follower buy into a free white, so my white lead never shrank while I banked 10 at a time. The moment that settled it was round III: I took Makeover so Cal couldn't rearrange his pile into white, bought Heiresses before Cal could, fired it for 7 white, then cast it out on Estate Sale for 9 more and Farewelled Dyer for 7 followers. Cash In on the last placement with nobody else holding white was 12 followers plus the +10 for free.

FEEL: Splurge | 2 | 3 | yes | Fine as a last-placement pickup; +1 per 2 paid is small next to Allowance.
FEEL: Exchange | 2 | 2 | yes | Two followers per resource reads well, but it's capped so low it's mostly a filler space.
FEEL: Farewell | 4 | 5 | yes | Casting out a 1-follower Dyer for its full 7 cost felt great, maybe too great, and I took it partly to deny Ava's Mentor for 9.
FEEL: Estate Sale | 5 | 5 | yes | Biggest swing in the game: a spent once-per-game Heiresses paid her full 9 cost back as white, and it was also Ava's only route into white.
FEEL: Cash In | 4 | 5 | yes | Perfect last-placement space; the +1 white it hands back means you keep the contest if nobody else has white, which feels like a loophole.
FEEL: Tryout | 3 | 3 | yes | Clever, Ava used Cashier through it nicely, but it's only as good as the shop row.
FEEL: Gather | 3 | 3 | yes | Plain red plus a recruit bonus; Cal used it well, never a dilemma for me.
FEEL: Walk-In | 2 | 2 | yes | Handing every rival a red and drawing blind was a gamble; once Old Maid sat in the deck, nobody wanted it.
FEEL: Promote | 4 | 3 | yes | With Recruiter it's +5 red and a stolen member, which is strong; it took my Alchemists and it stung.
FEEL: Demote | 4 | 3 | yes | Same as Promote; the pair plus Recruiter plus Deprogrammers gave Cal three gains off one swap.
FEEL: Recruit a Member | 2 | 3 | yes | A free member at 8 or less is nice but felt routine.
FEEL: Harvest | 3 | 3 | no | Picking any colors makes it a generic resource space more than a yellow one; Ava used it all on red once.
FEEL: Trade Seeds | 5 | 4 | yes | The real yellow choke point: taking it was mostly about stopping a rival swapping a pile back into yellow.
FEEL: Dilute | 5 | 5 | yes | My favourite space; three changes on a leader decides the yellow contest in round I and II, but where you put the changed resources is a real dilemma since it feeds another contest.
FEEL: Big Dilute | 4 | 4 | yes | Six changes is huge reach; Cal cleared me out of yellow with it, though both players who used it wasted changes on the shifting option list.
FEEL: Melting Pot | 3 | 3 | yes | Good value with three member colors, and late it's the last yellow space to deny.
FEEL: Makeover | 5 | 4 | yes | In round III it's as much a defensive block as a gain; whoever holds a big mixed pile can steal any contest with it.
FEEL: Money Changers | 5 | 5 | yes | Strongest artifact here: a free white on every follower buy, mine or a rival's, means a 1-follower buy with white costs nothing and white is never contested.
FEEL: Guest Book | 2 | 2 | yes | The artifact I'd least want: three colors cap it at a couple of triggers, and I could deny it by buying the cheap Volunteer.
FEEL: Volunteer | 3 | 3 | yes | Bought for 1 mostly so Ava couldn't use it to fire Guest Book; a blocker's buy.
FEEL: Shopkeeper | 4 | 4 | yes | Picked it over Martyrs; +2 white now and every round start was the backbone of my white lead.
FEEL: Martyrs | 3 | 2 | yes | Three followers for 4 is tempting but nothing at the table was going to make it leave, so the ability is blank.
FEEL: Dyer | 3 | 3 | yes | Good yellow seed for round III, then worth more as Farewell fodder than as a member, which says something about Farewell.
FEEL: Heiresses | 5 | 5 | yes | Bought it partly so Cal with 11 members couldn't, then used and cast it out for 16 white total, which is too much.
FEEL: Alchemists | 3 | 3 | unsure | 5 for 3 followers and 3 members was good value, until Cal Promoted it straight out of my cult.
FEEL: HR | 2 | 2 | unsure | 10 for a flat 4 never beat buying 10 followers outright.
FEEL: Cashier | 3 | 3 | yes | I never bought it, but it sitting in the shop made Tryout a real white-to-followers threat I had to watch.
META: The contests really are the game; whoever can choke a color's last spaces wins it, and the three-player wheel has few enough yellow and white spaces that a blocker can lock them. What's working: Dilute, Trade Seeds and Makeover make yellow a real tug of war, and Promote/Demote with Recruiter gave Cal a live counter. What isn't: Money Changers makes white uncontestable for whoever holds it, and Farewell/Estate Sale paying a member's full cost, even on a spent once-per-game card, is a huge swing. First thing I'd change is to have Farewell and Estate Sale pay half the cost, or have Money Changers trigger only on rivals' buys.
post.2:
I finished second with 69 to Ben's 93; Ben won it on the white engine, and I was never really in it after round I. I lost all three round I contests by spending my red on cheap bodies, then my round II Big Dilute backfired: I funneled both rivals' resources around and Ben immediately Diluted my yellow and rebuilt, so I gave up a +6 for nothing. The deciding stretch was Ben's round III: Heiresses paid 7 white, then Estate Sale cast her out for 9 more white and Farewell cast out Dyer for 7 followers, and with Money Changers refunding a white on every follower buy and Cash In at the end, white was unreachable. My comeback came from Recruiter on Promote/Demote (+5 red per rival swap) and a free Patriarch off Recruit a Member that scored 8 on 16 members. I also fumbled two multi-step choices because the option list renumbers between picks.

META: The contest-per-color structure and the red swap spaces work well; there are real fights over who holds what at the end of a round, and Dilute makes holding piles risky. White is too self-feeding: Money Changers refunds on every buy at the table, Shopkeeper and Heiresses pile white, and Farewell/Estate Sale pay full cost for a member already used up, so Ben ran away 93 to 69. First change: make Farewell and Estate Sale pay half cost (or exclude once-per-game members already used), then watch Money Changers. Also, the option list renumbering between picks inside one action caused misclicks for two of us.
